mainTopic: Partitions in water, tied boats and עירוב, partitions made on שבת, and how strong the tie between boats must be
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of a hanging partition (מחיצה תלויה), which the חכמים allowed only in water. It concludes that fish swimming under the partition do not count as breaking it. The גמרא then asks why the משנה needs to say that tied boats may be carried between. רבא says it means carrying through a small boat in the middle. רב ספרא rejects that and says the משנה teaches that the tied boats need an עירוב. A ברייתא supports him: if the boats come apart and are retied, or mats are rolled up and spread out again, the permission returns, because any partition made on שבת counts as a partition. The גמרא answers a challenge from רב נחמן by explaining that his limit on carrying is only a penalty for someone who made the partition on purpose. Finally, שמואל teaches that even a thin cloak-string that can hold the boats is enough for שבת, because there it is only a sign. An iron chain is required only for טומאה, because metal is treated like a dead body.

steps.title: A hanging partition works only in water
steps.stepSummary: The previous statement ends: a hanging partition (מחיצה תלויה) is valid only in water, as a special leniency of the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: …except in water; it is a leniency that the חכמים were lenient with regard to water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a statement that started on the previous amud. A partition that hangs down without reaching the ground counts as a wall only in water, because the חכמים were lenient there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a wall must reach the ground, or come within three טפחים of it, to count as a מחיצה. Over water, the חכמים allowed even a hanging partition. This is a special leniency for water only, not a general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A hanging partition that does not reach the ground

phrases.english: except in water,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous amud: a hanging partition lets you carry only over water.

phrases.english: it is a leniency that the Sages were lenient with water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hanging partition is valid only over water, as a special leniency of the חכמים.

steps.title: But fish swim under the partition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the leniency: fish pass under the hanging partition, so it should count as broken through.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why? Isn't there the passage of fish?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how a hanging partition in water can work at all. Fish swim right under it and 'break through' it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A partition that animals or people regularly pass through is usually not a real wall, because it has a breach (בקיעה). Fish constantly swim under the hanging partition, so it should be considered breached. The question is how the leniency could exist given that problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaching or passing through (which can cancel a partition)

phrases.english: And why? Isn't there the passage of fish?
phrases.notes: Fish swim under the hanging partition and 'breach' it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the water leniency stated in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The validity of a hanging partition over water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Passage under a partition normally breaks it, and fish pass under constantly.

steps.title: Fish passing through is not a breach
steps.stepSummary: Because the leniency clearly exists, the גמרא concludes that fish swimming through does not count as breaking the partition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: the passage of fish is not considered passage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by drawing a conclusion. Since the חכמים did allow the hanging partition, fish passing under it must not count as a breach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reasons backwards from the established rule. The leniency exists, so fish passage must not cancel a partition. 'שמע מינה' shows a new principle being learned from an existing law.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (a conclusion is drawn)

steps.whatToRemember: A hanging partition works over water, and fish swimming under it do not count as breaking it.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this —
the passage of fish is not considered passage.
phrases.notes: Fish passing through do not break the partition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 2 by deriving a principle.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בקיעת דגים לא שמה בקיעה: fish passing through does not breach a partition.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about tied boats
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: boats tied together may be carried between.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. It is setting up a question about this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full line in the משנה says that boats tied together allow carrying from one to the other on שבת. 'כו׳' tells us to supply the rest of the משנה's words.

phrases.english: Boats that are tied, etc.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה: one may carry from one to the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Boats tied together allow carrying from one to the other.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to teach something so obvious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for stating something that seems obvious. Tied boats are clearly joined, so why say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Boats tied together seem like one connected area. The challenge is that the משנה teaches nothing new. An answer must show what new point the משנה is making.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
phrases.notes: The boats are tied, so of course one may carry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the משנה quoted in step 4 is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the משנה's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Tied boats are obviously connected, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: רבא: it teaches carrying through a small middle boat
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה comes to permit carrying by way of a small boat between the two big ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is needed only to permit the small boat that is between them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the 'obvious' question by giving the משנה a new point. The משנה teaches that one may carry across using a small boat in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, the new point is not that the big boats are connected. It is that a small boat (ביצית) lying between them also counts, so one may pass objects through it. That would explain why the משנה needed to speak.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for… (introduces the משנה's real point)

phrases.english: Rava said:
It was needed only
phrases.notes: The משנה is needed for this point.

phrases.english: to permit the small boat that is between them.
phrases.notes: Carrying via a small boat in between.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the משנה a new case, so its statement is no longer obvious
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה only teaches that tied boats are connected, which is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that one may carry through a small boat between the two.

steps.title: רב ספרא: the משנה says 'from one to the other'
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא rejects רבא's answer because the משנה's wording speaks of carrying directly from one boat to the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said to him: משה, are you speaking well?! We learned 'one may carry from this one to that one'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא pushes back on רבא. The wording of the משנה does not fit the idea of a middle boat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'מזו לזו', from this one to that one, which means directly between the two boats. If it were teaching about a small boat in the middle, it would have said so. Calling רבא 'משה' is a term of respect, as if to say: someone as great as you, did you really say this?

keyTerms.meaning: From this one to that one

steps.confusionAlert: Calling רבא 'משה' is not mockery or a mistake about his name. It is an expression of honor, comparing a great sage to משה רבינו.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said to him:
Moshe, are you speaking well?!
phrases.notes: A respectful form of address used while objecting.

phrases.english: We learned 'one may carry from this one to that one'!
phrases.notes: This means directly between the two boats, not through a middle boat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סָפְרָא: מֹשֶׁה, שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרַתְּ
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The explanation that the משנה refers to a small middle boat
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's wording 'מזו לזו' refers to direct carrying between the two boats.

steps.title: רב ספרא: the משנה teaches that an עירוב is needed
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא explains that the משנה's point is that the tied boats require an עירוב before one may carry between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב ספרא said: It is needed only to make an עירוב and carry from one to the other.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא gives his own answer to the 'obvious' question. The משנה teaches that tied boats can be joined by an עירוב, which then allows carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The boats belong to different people, so each is a separate private domain. Tying them makes them close enough to join with an עירוב. The new point is that carrying needs an עירוב, and tying is what makes the עירוב possible.

keyTerms.meaning: To make an עירוב (joining separate domains)

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Safra said:
It was needed only
to make an eiruv and carry from one to the other,
phrases.notes: The tied boats need an עירוב to be treated as one domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's rejected answer with a new explanation of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה either states the obvious or refers to a middle boat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that tied boats may be joined by an עירוב, allowing carrying between them.

steps.title: ברייתא: tied boats need an עירוב, and retying restores it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב ספרא. Tied boats are joined by an עירוב; if they come apart, carrying is forbidden; if retied in any way, the permission returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Boats tied to one another, one makes an עירוב and carries from one to the other. If they were separated, they are forbidden. If they were tied again, whether unwittingly or intentionally, whether forced or mistaken, they return to their original permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב ספרא said. It also adds what happens if the boats come apart and are tied again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that tied boats need an עירוב, which supports רב ספרא. If the rope breaks, the boats are no longer joined, so carrying between them stops. Once they are retied, the original עירוב works again, no matter how the retying happened.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: 'נאסרו' does not mean the boats themselves become forbidden. It means carrying between them becomes forbidden while they are apart.

phrases.english: and as it was taught:
phrases.notes: What comes next is a ברייתא that backs this up.

phrases.english: boats tied to one another —
one makes an eiruv and carries from one to the other.
If they were separated, they are forbidden.
If they were tied again,
whether unwittingly or intentionally,
whether forced or mistaken —
they return to their original permission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב ספרא's explanation in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רב ספרא's claim that tied boats require an עירוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating 'ספינות קשורות זו בזו מערבין ומטלטלין מזו לזו'

steps.title: The same rule for mats spread as partitions
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא applies the same rule to mats spread out as partitions facing the public domain. If they are rolled up, carrying is forbidden; if spread out again in any way, the permission returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, mats spread out toward the public domain: one makes an עירוב and carries from one to the other. If they were rolled up, they are forbidden. If they were spread out again, whether unwittingly or intentionally, whether forced or mistaken, they return to their original permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second, parallel case: mats that act as walls. It applies the same rule as for the boats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the mats serve as partitions that close off an area from the רשות הרבים, allowing an עירוב and carrying. Rolling them up removes the partition, so carrying stops. Spreading them out again brings back the original permission, even if done on purpose.

phrases.english: And similarly, mats spread out toward the public domain —
one makes an eiruv and carries from one to the other.
If they were rolled up, they are forbidden.
If they were spread out again,
whether unwittingly or intentionally,
whether forced or mistaken —
they return to their original permission,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא extends the boat rule to a parallel case of mats.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mats serving as partitions allow an עירוב; rolling them up forbids carrying, and spreading them again restores the permission.

steps.title: Any partition made on שבת counts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives the reason: any partition made on שבת, whether by accident or on purpose, is a valid partition.
steps.simpleTranslation: For any partition that is made on שבת, whether unwittingly or intentionally, is considered a partition.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by explaining why retying the boats or spreading the mats restores the permission. A partition counts even if it was made on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a partition on שבת on purpose may itself be an improper act. Even so, the partition still works as a wall for the laws of carrying. That is why the original עירוב permission comes back once the boats are retied or the mats are spread out.
steps.whatToRemember: Tied boats need an עירוב to carry between them (רב ספרא). If the connection is broken and restored, even deliberately on שבת, the permission returns, because any partition made on שבת counts as a partition.
steps.confusionAlert: Even a partition made deliberately (במזיד) on שבת still counts. Whether the act of making it was proper does not change its status as a wall.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a broad principle: whether a wall counts depends on whether it physically exists, not on how or when it was made.

phrases.english: for any partition that is made on Shabbat,
whether unwittingly or intentionally —
is considered a partition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind both cases in the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Any partition made on שבת, accidentally or deliberately, counts as a valid partition.

steps.title: Challenge from רב נחמן: a partition made on שבת works only for throwing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that a partition made on שבת is valid. It quotes רב נחמן, who said this rule applies only to throwing, but carrying inside is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רב נחמן said: They only taught this rule regarding throwing, but carrying is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from the end of the ברייתא, that any partition made on שבת counts. It brings רב נחמן, who seems to limit that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא let people carry between boats that were retied on שבת. רב נחמן says a partition made on שבת counts only to make someone liable for throwing into it. It does not permit carrying. That seems to contradict the permission to carry between retied boats.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? An opening word for a challenge
They only taught this regarding... (limits a rule)
To throw (from one domain into another)
To carry or move objects within the area

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן does not deny that the partition is real. He only says carrying inside it is forbidden. The next step explains why.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rav Nachman say:
They only taught this regarding throwing,
phrases.notes: A partition made on שבת makes a real domain, so one who throws into it is liable.

phrases.english: but to carry is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's conclusion in step 11 that a partition made on שבת is fully valid.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that any partition made on שבת, by accident or on purpose, is a valid partition that permits carrying.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן limits such partitions to the law of throwing and forbids carrying, which contradicts the ברייתא's permission to carry between boats retied on שבת.

steps.title: רב נחמן was speaking about someone who made the partition on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב נחמן's ruling was said about a person who made the partition deliberately (מזיד). He is penalized and may not carry.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב נחמן's statement was said, it was said about someone who acted on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge. רב נחמן's limit applies only to someone who put up the partition on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who deliberately builds a partition on שבת is penalized and cannot benefit from it by carrying. The partition itself still counts as a real partition. So רב נחמן's limit is a penalty for acting on purpose, and it does not deny the ברייתא's principle that a partition made on שבת is a partition.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a partition made on שבת is valid in principle. Any limit on carrying is a penalty for acting deliberately, not a flaw in the partition itself.

phrases.english: When the statement of Rav Nachman was said —
it was said about one who acted intentionally.
phrases.notes: A penalty (קנס) for doing it on purpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אִיתְּמַר דְּרַב נַחְמָן אַמֵּזִיד אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 by limiting רב נחמן's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): רב נחמן is speaking about someone who acted deliberately.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן meant that a partition made on שבת never permits carrying.
steps.terutzMaskana: Carrying is forbidden only as a penalty for someone who made the partition deliberately. An accidental partition permits carrying.

steps.title: שמואל: even a cloak-string is enough to tie the boats
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the boats count as tied together, so carrying between them is allowed, even if they are tied with a thin string from a cloak.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: And even if they are tied with the string of a cloak.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: שמואל teaches that the tie between the boats can be as thin as a cloak's string.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we heard only that the boats must be tied. שמואל adds that the tie does not need to be heavy or strong-looking. A simple string from a garment counts.

keyTerms.meaning: The string of a cloak, a thin cord used to close a garment

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
And even if they are tied with the string of a cloak.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל וַאֲפִילּוּ קְשׁוּרוֹת בְּחוּט הַסַּרְבָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new point about how strong the tie between the boats must be.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Boats tied even with a thin cloak-string are considered joined, so carrying between them is permitted.

steps.title: What case is שמואל talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל means. If the string can hold the boats, his point is obvious. If it cannot hold them, why should it work?
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the circumstances? If the string can hold them in place, it is obvious. If it cannot hold them, why does it work?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל with a two-sided question. Either way, his statement seems unnecessary or wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the string really holds the boats together, then they are tied, and there is nothing new to say. If the string is too weak to hold them, it should not count as a tie at all. So what is שמואל teaching?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
To hold them in place (keep the boats together)
It is obvious (so why say it?)

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If it is able to hold them — it is obvious.
If it is not able to hold them — why should it work?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דְּיָכוֹל לְהַעֲמִידָן פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of שמואל's statement in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that a cloak-string is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dilemma: if the string holds the boats, the ruling is obvious. If it does not, the ruling makes no sense.

steps.title: The string does hold them; שמואל is contrasting with his own other ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the string really can hold the boats. שמואל said this to set it apart from another ruling of his own, about טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it is a case where it can hold them. And שמואל comes to exclude this from his own other statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks the first side: the string holds the boats. It explains that the ruling is not obvious, because שמואל himself was strict in a different area. The next step quotes that ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not obvious, because elsewhere שמואל required something much stricter, an iron chain. Without this statement, we might have thought שבת needs the same. שמואל is telling us that for שבת, any string that holds is enough.

phrases.english: Actually, it is where it is able to hold them.
And Shmuel comes to exclude it from his own statement.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם דְּיָכוֹל לְהַעֲמִידָן וּשְׁמוּאֵל לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדְּנַפְשֵׁיהּ קָאָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by choosing the 'can hold' side and explaining why it is not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the novelty: the ruling is set against שמואל's own stricter ruling elsewhere.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling is obvious if the string holds the boats.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is not obvious, because שמואל required an iron chain for טומאה. Here he teaches that שבת is more lenient.

steps.title: The משנה about טומאה and שמואל's iron-chain ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a boat tied to something in a tent with a dead body becomes טמא only if the tie can hold it. שמואל said that means an iron chain.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: If he tied it with something that holds it, it brings טומאה to it. With something that does not hold it, it does not bring טומאה to it. And שמואל said: That is when it is tied with an iron chain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the other ruling of שמואל that it mentioned in the previous step. For טומאה, שמואל requires an iron chain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the tie carries טומאה from a tent with a dead body to the boat, but only if the tie can hold the boat. שמואל narrows this to an iron chain. That is the strict standard he is now distinguishing from שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Brings ritual impurity to it (the boat)

phrases.english: As we learned: If he tied it with something that holds it —
phrases.notes: The other end of the tie is in a tent with a dead body.

phrases.english: it brings impurity to it.
With something that does not hold it —
it does not bring impurity to it.
And Shmuel said:
And that is when it is tied with an iron chain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source of 'his own statement' mentioned in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For טומאה, a boat tied to a tent with a dead body becomes טמא only if it is tied with an iron chain.

steps.title: Why טומאה needs iron but שבת accepts any string
steps.stepSummary: For טומאה, the פסוק teaches that metal is like a dead body (חרב הרי הוא כחלל), so only an iron chain works. For שבת, the tie is only a sign, so even a cloak-string that can hold the boats is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is for טומאה, as it is written 'בחלל חרב': a sword is like a dead body. But for שבת, since it can hold the boat, it is only a sign, so even a cloak-string is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the difference between שמואל's two rulings and finishes the topic. שבת is lenient, and טומאה is strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The iron chain matters for טומאה because metal touching a dead body takes on the body's own level of טומאה, based on the פסוק. That is a special law about metal, not about strength. For שבת, all we need is a sign (היכר) that the boats are joined, so any string that holds them counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A sword (metal) is like a dead body for טומאה

steps.whatToRemember: A partition made on שבת is valid, and only someone who made it on purpose is penalized. Tied boats may be joined for carrying with any tie that holds them, even a cloak-string, because for שבת the tie is just a sign. The iron chain is required only for טומאה, because of חרב הרי הוא כחלל.
steps.confusionAlert: The iron chain is not required because it is stronger. It is required because metal has a special טומאה status. That is why the rule does not carry over to שבת.

phrases.english: That is regarding impurity,
as it is written: 'one slain by a sword' —
a sword is like the slain (the dead body).
phrases.notes: Metal touching a dead body takes on the body's level of impurity.

phrases.english: (Yes,) but regarding Shabbat,
since it is able to hold it,
it is merely a sign —
even with the string of a cloak.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For שבת, any tie that can hold the boats, even a cloak-string, joins them, because it serves only as a sign. An iron chain is needed only for טומאה, because metal is like a dead body.
